latest_release.name: Termix v26.11.3
latest_release.body:
> [!TIP]
> Termix is free and always will be. If it's useful to you, consider [donating](https://donate.termix.site/donate/) to support development.

### Added

- Diagnostics report: one file with errors, logs, plugin states and connection checks to attach to a bug report. Names and addresses are hidden by default and secrets are always removed. Open it from a plugin's page, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D, the login page, a slow loading screen, or any Termix address with ?diagnostics added
- Admins can watch the server log live in the diagnostics page
- Admins can let community layouts and themes run outside the sandbox again, behind a warning, in Plugins, Registries
- Set SERVE_OPENAPI=true to serve this server's own API spec at /version/openapi.json: core and every plugin that is on, at the versions it runs, with the server's address filled in
- Access plugins can end the connections already open to a host when its access ends, and can keep status checks from contacting it
- Desktop app: termix:// links open the app. termix://host/<id> connects to a saved host after asking, and a shortcut with --host=<id> opens straight into it
- Quick Connect can use a saved credential, resolved on the server so its password never reaches the browser
- Confirm prompts can have a checkbox, like Delete permanently in the file manager
- Host row badges from plugins can show an icon and their own color
- Dashboard cards from plugins let the layout's card color show behind them
- Signing out can also sign you out of your single sign on provider, when its login method asks for it
- Desktop app: logins of web pages a plugin shows in the app are kept across reloads and reopened tabs until Termix quits or you sign out. Pages on this computer still start signed out
- Setup has a Pick a layout step that shows every installed layout with a screenshot and a link to its video. Admins can also install layouts from the registry or turn on ones that are off
- Layouts with a host tree can list what runs inside a host, like containers and guests, under it

### Fixed

- Signing out from the menu ends the session on the server too, not only in the browser
- Embedded web pages from plugins, like Homepage iFrame widgets, show again in Safari and Firefox when the page is on another host
- Desktop app: parts of plugins that only show in the desktop app, like a local terminal, show again
- Plugins that are blocked or stopped after an upgrade show their update again, and Update all no longer greys out when only those are left
- Update all opens a review for each plugin whose update asks for new permissions, instead of skipping it without a word
- When a login proxy in front of Termix blocks plugin files, Termix says so and links to the fix, instead of showing "Getting plugins ready" on every load
- A plugin that can't read its own files says which folder and how to fix it, instead of "did not start"
- A blocked plugin says "Can't start" with the reason, instead of always "Waiting on another plugin" even when it only needs an update
- The plugin loading screen no longer says it only shows the first time
- The loading screen stays up until plugins are ready, so buttons and rail items no longer pop in and host details no longer flash right after it
- Plugins can write to files they saved before 26.11.2 again, like Session Recording's recordings
- The first plugin installed from the store on a new install starts without a restart
- A terminal's tab shows its Share button and Share menu entry again, and Refresh connection, Reconnect all and focus in split screen work on it again
- Shared session links open again, for people with or without an account
- A plugin that stops right as Termix sends it a message can no longer crash the whole server
- Desktop app: plugin updates no longer fail with "inclusion promise could not be verified", thanks to dean for finding the cause
- Termix starts again when the data folder doesn't allow changing file owners,

detail.readme:
Termix

Self-hosted, plugin-based server management


## Overview Termix is a free, open source, self-hosted server management platform built on plugins. The core keeps your hosts, credentials, users, sharing and sessions. Everything else, like the SSH terminal, remote desktop, file manager, Docker and metrics, is a plugin you can turn on, off or remove. It runs on web, desktop and mobile. Think of it as a free, self-hosted Termius.
## Try the Demo Try it at [demo.termix.site](https://demo.termix.site/). Any username and password works.
## Core What every install has, with or without plugins: - Hosts: Save hosts in nested folders with tags and parent hosts, bulk edit, import and export, and use Quick Connect for one-off connections - Credentials: Reuse saved passwords and keys across hosts, with host defaults you can set for the server, a user or a folder - Sharing and Roles: Share hosts, credentials and folders with users or roles at four levels: connect, view, edit and manage - Accounts: Local accounts, sessions you can see and revoke, trusted devices, API keys and an audit log - Security: Passwords, keys and other secrets are encrypted per user, and the database can be encrypted on disk - Desktop Sync: The desktop app runs on its own and can link to a Termix server to keep an offline copy of your account - Interface: Tabs and split screen, a command palette (double tap left shift), rebindable shortcuts, themes, branding and around 30 languages - Databases: SQLite by default, with PostgreSQL and MySQL supported too
## Plugins Plugins add everything else. Admins can install, update or remove plugins from the Plugins tab, and each plugin has its own repo. These ship in the default image: | Plugin | What it does | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | Want to build your own? Start from the [plugin template](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Plugin-Template). Plugins you can install are listed in the [registry](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Registry). Turn on the community registry in Plugins, Registries to install plugins made by other people, or add your own registry. See [submitting a plugin](https://docs.termix.site/develop/community-registry) and [hosting your own registry](https://docs.termix.site/develop/registries#host-your-own-registry).
## Platform Support
Platform Distribution
Web Any modern browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) | PWA support
Windows x64/arm64 Portable | EXE and MSI Installer | Full EXE (all plugins) | Chocolatey
Linux x64/arm64 Portable | AUR | AppImage | Deb | Full AppImage and Deb (all plugins) | Flatpak
macOS Universal/x64/arm64, v12.0+ Apple App Store | DMG | Full DMG (all plugins) | Homebrew
iOS/iPadOS v15.1+ Apple App Store | IPA
Android v7.0+ Google Play Store | APK

## Installation See the [docs](https://docs.termix.site/install) for install steps on every platform. On macOS, Termix, Menu Bar Icon picks a monochrome icon (the default), a color icon or no icon. The choice is saved on this device. With the icon hidden, open Termix from the Dock to change it back, and closing the last window quits the app. Sample Docker Compose file. Remote desktop (RDP, VNC and Telnet) is built in, so nothing else needs to run next to it: ```yaml services: termix: image: ghcr.io/termix-ssh/termix:latest container_name: termix restart: unless-stopped ports: - "8080:8080" volumes: - termix-data:/app/data environment: PORT: "8080" volumes: termix-data: driver: local ``` ### Cloud Hosting If Termix runs on the network it manages, an outage takes it down right when you need it. A VPS keeps it reachable, gives you a static IP and works from anywhere without a VPN or port forward. [GINERNET](https://docs.termix.site/install/ginernet) sponsors Termix and the docs have a setup guide for their VPS.
## Donate Termix has no paid plans. Donations cover servers, domains and development time. [Donate](https://donate.termix.site/)
## Sponsors For a paid sponsor spot, email [mail@termix.site](mailto:mail@termix.site).

                           

## Support Bugs and ideas for Termix itself (login, hosts, credentials, sharing, sync, the app and desktop app) go in this repo: [report a bug](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) or [request a feature](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml). Every plugin has its own repo, so a problem with the terminal, file manager, Docker, remote desktop or any other plugin goes in that plugin's repo (see the table above, or use Report an issue on the plugin's page in the app, which fills in your versions for you). Not sure where it goes? Open it here and it will be moved. You need a GitHub account. Add as much detail as you can, in English if possible. For discussions and questions, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jVQGdvHDrf) server. Update videos are on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@TermixSSH/videos).
